speaker: Quill
text: Oh. Oh, you hear it too. Forgive me, I’m— Quill. Night archivist. Nobody asks what an archivist does at night, which is lucky, because mostly it’s listening. ... I have waited fifty years for someone else to hear it.

speaker: Quill
text: Not tonight. The bell is hungry, and you are rather small to feed it. Come to the archive tomorrow. Bring questions. Bring tea, if you can steal any.

speaker: Harrow
text: Sleepwalkers don’t carry wands.

speaker: Mirela
text: Four last night. Six tonight, ... Asleep, all of them. Calm as lambs, cold as slate. The staff are calling it a stomach bug. ... I call it something else.

speaker: Mirela
text: You heard the bell. Most people don’t. That makes you either very useful or very unlucky. Possibly both.

speaker: Mirela
text: Tolls every eleven minutes, sometimes ten. It’s speeding up. ... I’d like to know if it’s locked or just unwelcoming.

speaker: Mirela
text: Interesting, ... You held on longer than I would have.

speaker: Mirela
text: That, ... is not a lock.

speaker: Mirela
text: Well, ... It listens, at least.

speaker: Matron Hale
text: Sleeping sickness, ... Nothing to be done but rest and fluids. Professor Ashgrove has been very kind about it.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: I need your word that you won’t go after that bell on your own, and that you won’t draw other students into this. For their safety. And yours.

speaker: Mirela
text: The tower was sealed fifty years ago and there’s not a line in the school records about why, ... I think I know how to stop it. I need someone with nerve. ... Congratulations. You volunteered.

speaker: Harrow
text: You followed someone with keys, ... And you think it was me.

speaker: Harrow
text: It was me, ... Every night since the first sleeper. Because if somebody doesn’t watch that door, somebody worse than me will.

speaker: Harrow
text: We’ll say no more about it, ... You’ve got enough on your plate.

speaker: Harrow
text: I was a junior caretaker the night it started, fifty years back. I saw a boy in an archive coat carry music out of the east wing and lock the door behind him. He was crying. I never asked who it was.

speaker: Harrow
text: Opens most doors in the east and west wings. You never had it, understand?

speaker: Mirela
text: I’ve done the arithmetic, ... It’s speeding up. At this rate the whole castle is asleep in four days.

speaker: Mirela
text: I have a plan, and you won’t like it. I found a counter-spell in an old book that can break metal like this. We take the bell. ... But I don’t know what lies under that tower. I only know I can’t watch one more person fall asleep.

speaker: Mirela
text: Fine. But if there’s nothing else by tonight, we take the bell. No more talking.

speaker: Quill
text: Ah! My night visitor. Sit. Mind the cat; she bites scholars.

speaker: Quill
text: You’re late, ... Or early. It rather depends what you’re looking for.

speaker: Quill
text: Hollow Bell. Cast three hundred years ago by Cantor Eadric Vale, who led the castle choir. It was never meant to warn anyone. It was meant to hold something down.

speaker: Quill
text: Beneath the tower lies what we call the Hush. It eats sound, and it eats sleep. Vale sang it to rest every night with a song that closes the bell. Then the song was lost, and the bell began to ring by itself. Now it feeds on whoever sleeps.

speaker: Quill
text: The song was written on two pages. I know where one of them is.

speaker: Quill
text: The bell will ring itself if the song is forgotten. Remember that the song is written on two pages.

speaker: Quill
text: You’re looking for the bell, aren’t you? ... You look so innocent that you very nearly fooled me.

speaker: Quill
text: I wasn’t always an archivist. Fifty years ago I was Vale’s last student, seventeen years old. The night the bell began ringing by itself, I panicked. I tore out the page with the song and locked the music room. I thought that would stop it.

speaker: Quill
text: It did the opposite. Since then I have been an archivist, a watchman and a coward, all at once.

speaker: Quill
text: It’s in there somewhere, ... I can’t search any more. My eyes aren’t what they were.

speaker: Quill
text: The Cantor’s close. To be sung from the tower, and the bell shall be stilled.

speaker: Quill
text: Take it. And for heaven’s sake, don’t lose it.

speaker: Quill
text: That is as much as I have, ... Mind it well.

speaker: Quill
text: Somebody got here first, ... It’s not the first time something has disappeared from here.

speaker: Vale
text: No one has knocked here in a very long time, ... You are kind. Come in. I am Eadric Vale.

speaker: Vale
text: You come to take more! ... I have nothing left to give!

speaker: Vale
text: Now you know why I cannot sing alone, ... The song is true only if someone shares the price with me. I remember it all, child. The melody still lives in me. I merely cannot hold it up by myself.

speaker: Vale
text: My tuning fork. With it you can tune the bell to the lullaby. And if you find the pages, perhaps we can give them peace together.

speaker: Vale
text: There has been another here, ... The professor. Three times. He wants the song, but not to close the bell. He wants to use it to ring thirteen.

speaker: Vale
text: I said no. But he promises me my freedom if I sing. I am tired, child. I am so very tired.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: My sister Lenora climbed Hollow Tower when she was twelve, to prove she was brave. She fell asleep up there. She never woke.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: I was sixteen. I have spent the rest of my life trying to understand why.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: Come to me whenever you’re worried.

speaker: Mirela
text: What do we do if Ashgrove is up there? ... If he’s the one ringing, he’s the enemy.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: You gave me your word,

speaker: Ashgrove
text: I did not ask you to come, ... But now that you are here, I can at least explain.

speaker: Vale
text: I am sorry, ... But this is what I owe them.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: The Hush beneath us is the only reason this castle still stands, ... Every night it grows stronger. The bell holds it down, but it feeds on the sleepers. If I ring thirteen strokes, it seals for ever. The price is those who already sleep.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: Forty-one students for a thousand. I have done the arithmetic for ten years. I am not proud of it.

speaker: Quill
text: Corvin, ... It was I who tore out the page. It was I who locked the door. This is my responsibility. Don’t make it your students’.

speaker: Quill
text: You let them sleep for fifty years,

speaker: Quill
text: You? ... All these years?

speaker: Ashgrove
text: I have been set on this for ten years, ... And a child comes and shows me I stopped looking for anything else.

speaker: Ashgrove
text: I should have given you this long ago, ... The other half.

speaker: Vale
text: If you ask me to sing, I bind myself to the bell once more. I do it gladly. But I need something to sing from.

speaker: Vale
text: What are you doing?
